title: Explain AI to others
desc: Prepare and give a clear talk that teaches AI to a younger audience
content_html:
What We're Doing

Leaders can explain technology clearly — and understanding actually grows when you have to teach it to someone else. If you can explain AI simply, in plain words, you really understand it. In this lesson each learner prepares and delivers a short, jargon-free explanation of AI aimed at a specific audience, then improves it based on real feedback.

You'll Need

  • Paper and pens for drafting
  • A timer
  • Optional: a simple scoring sheet (Clear? / No jargon? / Could you repeat it back?)

Step-by-Step Activity

  1. Each learner chooses a specific audience — a parent, a younger sibling, or a head teacher.
  2. They write a three-sentence explanation of what AI is for that audience, with no jargon.
  3. In pairs, they practise delivering it out loud. The partner scores it: Was it clear? Any jargon? Could they repeat it back in their own words?
  4. Each learner iterates once, rewriting the weakest sentence based on that feedback.
  5. A few present to the whole group, and the audience proves it worked by repeating the idea back.

Examples

  • Jargon-heavy (weak): "AI leverages neural architectures to perform inference on multimodal inputs."
  • Clear (strong): "AI is a computer that learns from lots of examples, so it can make good guesses about new things it has never seen before."

Facilitation Tips

  • Ban five "jargon" words at the start (algorithm, neural network, model, data, inference) to force plain language.
  • The best test of understanding is the audience repeating it back — make that the real score.
  • Celebrate short and clear over long and impressive.

Discussion Questions

  • Why does teaching something to someone else deepen your own understanding?
  • How does your explanation change for a 6-year-old versus a head teacher?
  • What is one piece of jargon you used to use that you can now say in plain words?

Extension Challenges

  • Easy: Turn your explanation into a one-page poster for a younger class.
  • Medium: Record a 60-second video explaining AI to a family member.
  • Hard: Plan and deliver a 5-minute mini-lesson that actually teaches a younger class one true thing about AI.
